idiom_name: functools.total_ordering decorator plus collections.abc mixin classes
implementation_notes: Python defines operators as dunder methods and the standard library already supplies both halves of the idiom: functools.total_ordering fills in __gt__/__le__/__ge__ from one root method (__lt__, or __le__/__gt__/__ge__) plus __eq__, and the collections.abc mixin classes donate whole operator families to a family of types - Set provides __le__, __lt__, __gt__, __ge__ and the set operators once a class implements the three abstract methods. Multiple inheritance is the CRTP substitute (there is no static type parameter to pass), and @dataclass(order=True) generates the comparison methods for a whole class. Use total_ordering only for genuinely total orders: it derives the other operators by calling the root dunder directly, which costs an extra call and is slower and harder to debug than writing all six.
pitfalls: total_ordering derives the other comparisons by calling the root dunder plus __eq__, so each derived operator costs extra calls; on hot paths implement all six rich-comparison methods by hand.
Return NotImplemented (never False) for unsupported operand types, otherwise reflected dispatch is skipped and the expression fails with a confusing TypeError.
Defining __eq__ without __hash__ makes instances unhashable, and a mixin class inherited before another may shadow its operators in the MRO - ordering and hashing have to be reasoned about together.
